A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GIM study and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices. Renumbered appendix sections and relocated material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic causal-model experiments and SciPlex3 drug-perturbation evaluations in Section 6 and Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results in Section 6 and Appendix E, including causal discovery, intervention-target identification and distribution prediction.

M1.justification: The feature-to-intervention mapping, causal models, MAP objective, priors and optimization procedures are retained. Expanded graph-embedding explanations and notation do not establish an algorithmic change.

E1.justification: Both evaluate linear and nonlinear synthetic systems with ER and scale-free graphs, hard and shift interventions, and the same generalization scenarios. SciPlex3 coverage remains four drugs across three cell lines.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in corresponding experiments is unchanged: BaCaDI*, GnIES, UT-IGSP, both JCI-PC variants, MLP, CondOT, and observational or naive controls where applicable. Baseline implementation descriptions are also retained.

E3.justification: Section 5, the experimental-setup appendix and Tables 1–2 retain the same preprocessing, splits, metrics, architectures, training budgets and tuning procedures. This includes the synthetic sample counts and SciPlex3 highest-dose holdout protocol.

E4.justification: Both retain PCA feature-information sensitivity tests, the hyperparameter-selection comparison, shift-intervention and scale-free-graph evaluations, and intervention-effect and gene-expression case studies. Relocating these analyses into Appendix E adds no new analysis.

E5.justification: Both retain the same median and interquartile-range reporting, including boxplot whiskers extending to 1.5 times the IQR. Run-count, seed, confidence-interval and significance-reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: The plotted results in Figures 2–13 are identical, including distributions, rankings and qualitative examples. Their accompanying findings are retained, with no added, removed or corrected empirical results.

T1.justification: Section 4.2 adds a conditional large-sample identifiability argument applying prior results to GIMs and states a graph-representation expressivity property. New Appendix C supplies an asymptotic computational-cost expression. Existing model and gradient derivations remain substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract and the substantive introduction and conclusion claims are retained: GIMs connect perturbation features to atomic interventions, provide mechanistic insights and generalize competitively to unseen perturbations.

C2.justification: The new identifiability discussion qualifies recovery as training-target identification and recovery of an interventional Markov equivalence class, subject to model expressivity and prior-support conditions. Existing empirical interpretations and the dependence of generalization on informative features are retained.

D1.justification: Section 5 adds a stated code-availability link absent from v1. Existing preprocessing, hyperparameter and optimization details are retained in the renumbered experimental-setup appendix.

R1.justification: v2 newly connects GIM identifiability to Brouillard et al. and Yang et al., and compares computational complexity with Brouillard et al. and Hagele et al. The cited works themselves are retained; publication-year and venue updates are bibliographic changes.

P1.justification: Localized rewrites in Sections 2–4 clarify observed features, latent interventions and graph-embedding notation. Publication and affiliation information is updated, and the new complexity appendix shifts the former Appendices C–D to D–E without substantially reorganizing the narrative.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn with descriptive variable labels, biological examples and an expanded caption. Existing tables and experimental figures are redistributed across pages, while their scientific content and display structures are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 improves readability through clearer explanations and the annotated Figure 1, while identifiability conditions and computational-cost analysis make the method easier to assess. Added code-access information improves reproducibility documentation. These are limited gains: the theoretical justification remains brief and conditional, and the method and empirical evidence are preserved.
